Article Title: SC permits Congress delegation to file petition within premises as Rahul leads INDIA bloc march
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has permitted a delegation of 10-15 people from Congress party to go to the filing counter inside the premises as Rahul Gandhi leads INDIA bloc's march to the top court.However, the delegation would be outside the high-security zone to file their petition, sources told TOI.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi began his planned march to the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.The Congress MP called for the "Challo Dilli" protest march, which was planned from Connaught Place to the Supreme Court against the functioning of the poll body.The opposition continued the protest despite the CJI not giving his assent to a meeting with the opposition MPs on the issue.Earlier in the day, Rahul Gandhi also called for a news conference on the protest. In a post on X he said, "March for Democracy. March for Justice. Chalo Dilli."Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant, however, on Monday said every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court and that the Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone, amid the INDIA bloc's planned protest march to the court against the Election Commission.Responding to the INDIA bloc's request for a meeting, the CJI said he had received a letter on Sunday and replied to it the same night, explaining why he would not be able to meet the delegation."I received a letter yesterday regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet," CJI Surya Kant told reporters after NHRC's 33rd Foundation Day function.He also emphasised that any citizen or elected representative could approach the court and seek legal relief."The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law," he said.CJI Justice Surya Kant had earlier rejected the INDIA bloc leaders’ request for a meeting to submit a representation over alleged electoral irregularities, stating that they should approach the court by filing a petition as the matter is already sub judice.
Article Summary: 10-15 people from Congress party to go to the filing counter inside the premises as Rahul Gandhi leads INDIA bloc's march to the top court. The delegation would be outside the high-security zone to file their petition. Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant said every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court.

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has backed Rahul Gandhi 's call for the ouster of the current BJP government and the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar. Tharoor shared an excerpt from Ramdhari Singh Dinkar's popular poem, "(The Birth of Democracy).(Vacate the throne, for the people are coming!)," Tharoor shared in a post. Interestingly, these lines long echoed India's political corridors during the JP movement against the national Emergency imposed by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1975.Tharoor called it the poem of the day, coinciding with Rahul Gandhi's planned march to the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, who has been under fire from the opposition over his handling of the contentious Special Intensive Revision (SIR).“This government will go,” Tharoor also said in a previous post.In a show of opposition unity, a large demonstration led by INDIA bloc leaders and lawmakers wound its way through the streets of the national capital before reaching the Constitution Club of India.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, along with former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee , arrived at the Constitution Club.Rahul Gandhi had called on citizens to join the INDIA bloc's protest march towards the Supreme Court against alleged "vote theft".He said the alliance was moving to file a petition following directions from the Chief Justice of India (CJI).In a post on X with the hashtag #ChaloDilli, the Congress leader urged people to gather at Connaught Place in central Delhi to participate in the demonstration, which aims to safeguard democratic and constitutional values."We had written a letter to the CJI. He directed us to file a petition. Now, leaders of the INDIA alliance will march to the SupremeCourt against 'vote theft' and file the petition," Rahul Gandhi posted on X.Appealing for nationwide participation, he urged citizens to join the march in person or raise their voices from wherever they were."In this fight to protect democracy and the Constitution, fellow citizens, let us march step in step with us. Reach Connaught Place and become part of this march. If you can't come, raise your voice from wherever you are! #ChaloDilli," the LoP added.During the march, Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal launched a sharp attack on the central government, describing the opposition's agitation as the 'biggest andolan" against the poll panel and announcing that the party was taking its legal battle to the Supreme Court.'This is the biggest andolan against the Election Commissioner and the election system. Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are using the Chief Election Commissioner as their tool to destroy the democracy of this country, to hijack the democracy of the country," Venugopal said.
Article Summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has backed Rahul Gandhi's call for the ouster of the current BJP government and the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar. He shared an excerpt from Ramdhari Singh Dinkar's popular poem, "(The Birth of Democracy).(Vacate the throne, for the people are coming!)" The lines echoed India's political corridors during the JP movement against the national Emergency imposed by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1975.

Article Title: INDIA bloc fumes as CJI declines meeting request; Raut says ‘people will remember this’

NEW DELHI: Several opposition leaders from the INDIA bloc criticised Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant after he declined Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi’s request for a meeting to discuss alleged electoral fraud and the deletion of voters’ names from electoral rolls.Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut questioned the decision, saying the bloc wanted to raise concerns about “theft of votes” and the impact of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The opposition’s reaction came as the INDIA bloc has planned a protest march towards the Supreme Court on Monday.Raut said the Chief Justice’s refusal to meet the leaders would be remembered by the people, while Congress MP Imran Masood described the planned protest as a spontaneous movement.“We have come today as the INDIA bloc is organising a major march towards the Supreme Court to meet the Chief Justice. We had requested an appointment... The Chief Justice, whose role is to safeguard the Constitution, is unwilling to meet us... When we are seeking to save democracy amidst the theft of votes and electoral fraud, and the deletion of millions of names from the rolls and wish to meet you to voice our grievance, you say you will not meet politicians.The people will remember this,” Raut said.Congress MP Imran Masood also said the party had scheduled a protest and that members would follow the leadership’s directions.“We have scheduled a protest. Everyone will abide by whatever directive the party issues. People are coming out on their own; everywhere it is a spontaneous movement,” Masood said.Meanwhile, DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan questioned the circumstances behind the CJI’s decision to decline the meeting request and alleged that the Election Commission was not acting neutrally.“I do not know what pressure they are under... It is a petition in favour of democracy. We complain that Gyanesh Kumar is pro-BJP and he does not act neutrally... They should act neutrally, only then democracy will survive. If they are supporting Gyanesh Kumar, that means they are also against democracy...” Elangovan said.Responding to the meeting request, Justice Surya Kant said he had received a letter seeking an appointment on Sunday and had replied the same night, explaining why he would be unable to meet the leaders.“I received a letter yesterday regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet...” the CJI said.He also stressed that citizens and elected representatives could approach the court through legal channels.“The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law,” he said.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders from the INDIA bloc criticised Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant. He declined Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi’s request for a meeting to discuss alleged electoral fraud and the deletion of voters’ names from electoral rolls. Congress MP Imran Masood described the planned protest as a spontaneous movement.

NEW DELHI: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan on Monday blamed the Congress’s “directionless leadership” for its continued electoral defeats and criticised the opposition party for holding institutions such as the Election Commission (EC) responsible for its repeated losses.“Losing elections back-to-back and reacting by taking out protests and taking matters to the streets has become the fate of the Congress... The reason for this is not the Election Commission, but the directionless leadership of Congress itself,” Chouhan said at a press conference at the headquarters of the ruling BJP in the capital.He also cited recent instances of infighting within the Congress, including in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, as contributing to the party’s electoral setbacks.“There is continuous infighting in Uttar Pradesh, the state president in Punjab had to be changed, internal leadership feuds are ongoing in various places... It is the leadership of Congress—a leadership that does not know the country, its people,” Chouhan added.In Punjab, the Congress replaced Amarinder Singh Raja Warring with Pargat Singh as state unit president amid escalating tensions between Warring’s camp and that of former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi.In Uttar Pradesh, supporters of newly appointed state Congress chief Aradhana Misra clashed with those of her predecessor, Ajay Rai.Meanwhile, Chouhan further accused the grand old party of repeatedly targeting constitutional institutions over the years, alleging that the Congress had made it a "pattern" to blame these institutions for its defeats.“For several years, the Congress party has been continuously attacking constitutional institutions. It has reached a point where blaming constitutional institutions for election defeats has become a pattern,” he asserted.Chauhan described the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court to file a petition against the alleged "vote chori" (vote theft) by the BJP in "collusion" with the EC as a "drama.""Rahul Gandhi's march to SC to meet CJI is a drama. Kumar has also come under scrutiny following a media report claiming that the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had formally raised objections at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions they alleged were taken without their knowledge.
Article Summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan blamed the Congress’s “directionless leadership” for its continued electoral defeats. He also criticised the opposition party for holding institutions such as the Election Commission responsible for its repeated losses. His remarks came amid intensifying Congress protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar no longer a protest site; three new venues designated
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar no longer protest site

Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, CBD Ground named new protest sites

NEW DELHI: Jantar Mantar on Monday was denotified as a designated protest site, with three alternative venues designated for demonstrations in Delhi.In a notice issued by Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, the police said the ministry of home affairs had constituted a committee to examine suitable alternative venues for citizens to exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.The decision was taken based on the committee’s recommendations."Ministry of home affairs, Government of India, had constituted a Committee to examine alternative proper venues for citizen's right for organizing protest/demonstrations in place of the existing designated site. Based on the Committee's recommendations, Jantar Mantar as a protest venue has been de-notified," the notice reads.The three venues designated for organising protests and demonstrations are Ramlila ground in Central Delhi, Burari Ground in North Delhi and CBD Ground in East Delhi. The Delhi Police said a detailed and revised standard operating procedure (SOP) governing protests at the three venues would be issued separately.The order partially modifies the earlier Standing Order No. L&O/48/22, dated April 28, 2022."Detailed and revised SOP for organizing protest/demonstrations at these three venues will be issued separately. This is in partial modification of earlier Standing Order No.L&O/48/22 dated 28.04.2022," the notice reads further.The move comes amid ongoing massie protests in the national capital demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: Jantar Mantar denotified as a designated protest site. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, CBD Ground named new protest sites. Move comes amid ongoing massie protests in the national capital over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

NEW DELHI: Police in Uttar Pradesh’s Moradabad are investigating allegations that three men were illegally confined and tortured at the residence of BJP MLA Sushant Singh over a missing gold bracelet belonging to the legislator’s son, PTI reported citing officials.The complainants have sought the registration of an FIR against six named persons, including the MLA’s aides, and nine unidentified individuals. However, no case had been registered so far, Moradabad SP (Rural) Kunwar Akash Singh said, adding that action would be taken after an investigation.According to the victims’ family, Atul and Lavesh, who worked as domestic help at the legislator’s house, and their friend Ramu were held captive and tortured over the suspected theft of the gold bracelet.Ramu’s mother, Omwati, alleged that an aide of the MLA took her son from their home on October 7, while Atul and Lavesh were already being held at the residence.She claimed that the three men were hung upside down, beaten with belts, subjected to electric shocks and had salt rubbed into their wounds.All three were admitted to a hospital in Kashipur. Officials said Ramu’s condition was critical.Sushant Singh dismissed the allegations as baseless, maintaining that the domestic workers had only been questioned about the missing bracelet and had not been assaulted.Moradabad MP and Samajwadi Party leader Ruchi Veera demanded immediate justice for the victims and strict action against those responsible.Police said further action would follow the investigation.(With inputs from PTI)

Article Title: 'They are inconveniencing common public': Yogi Adityanath slams INDIA bloc for 'blaming EC when they lose'

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday slammed the Congress and the INDIA bloc amid their planned protest march against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, saying "it is surprising that if they win elections, it is their capability, but if they lose, they blame EVMs, EC. "Speaking to ANI, Adityanath urged the opposition to change its conduct and leadership, alleging that its response to election results reflected a lack of trust in constitutional bodies."They are inconveniencing the common public by creating anarchy. They are also attempting to question the constitutional institutions of the country. It is surprising that if they win elections, it is their capability. But if they lose, they blame EVMs, EC," he said."Such conduct has become part of Congress' intent. They should change their corrupt conduct and their distrustful leadership. They should not spread anarchy in India or attempt to question the constitutional bodies in India," he added.The UP chief minister further warned that people would not tolerate such actions for long and said the Congress could face political consequences if it continued with the same approach."People will not accept this anarchy, they will not tolerate this for long. If they continue like this, they will have to lose whatever they are left with," he added.Adityanath's remarks came as the INDIA bloc prepared to hold a protest march to the Supreme Court on Monday. Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi called on students, civil society organisations and opposition parties to join the march."12th October, India marches peacefully as one to the Supreme Court. Article Title: BJP Mahila Morcha protests against Congress MP Akoijam over harassment allegations, burns Rahul Gandhi's effigy

NEW DELHI: BJP Mahila Morcha workers staged protests across the country on Monday, burning effigies of leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam over allegations of sexual harassment involving female students at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).The protesters demanded action against Akoijam, who represents Inner Manipur in the Lok Sabha, and accused the Congress leadership of remaining silent over the allegations.BJP workers also marched towards the Congress office in Delhi, calling for the MP's removal and arrest.The protests followed reports that JNU had dismissed Akoijam from his position as a professor after an internal committee found allegations made by 11 female students to be true, according to the BJP. The allegations have not been independently verified in the material provided.Sharing a video on X, the BJP criticised the Congress leadership over its response to the allegations. BJP leader and MP Bansuri Swaraj questioned Rahul Gandhi's silence and challenged the party to take action against Akoijam.She said, “On October 9, 2026, a report from JNU's internal committee emerges, in which the allegations of sexual exploitation made by 11 female students against Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam are found to be true, and he is immediately dismissed from his job.“I want to ask Rahul Gandhi ji and the Congress... why have you remained silent until now? “Why haven't you taken action yet?“Rahul Gandhi ji, is ‘Smash The Patriarchy’ just an electoral slogan for you? “If not, then take action against Bimol Akoijam.”Swaraj also contrasted the BJP's position on women's political representation with her criticism of the Congress.“On one side is PM Shri Narendra Modi, who is increasing women's political representation through 'Women's Reservation.' On the other side is Rahul Gandhi, who obstructs even its implementation, gives a place in the Lok Sabha to a Sexual Predator, and provides protection to him through his silence,” she added.In another post, BJP MP Kamaljeet Sehrawat called on Rahul Gandhi to respond to the allegations."Rahul Gandhi should answer to those daughters who had come to India's renowned university (JNU) with trust. And today, a Congress MP himself is sexually exploiting them. These daughters, who are unsafe today, hold Rahul Gandhi and his party responsible."The BJP also questioned whether the Congress was living up to its stated commitment to women's safety.“Is Rahul Gandhi forgetting ‘Smash the Patriarchy’ now, or are the 'echoes of complaints' from 11 female students not reaching him?” the party said in a post.In another statement, the BJP alleged that Akoijam had been suspended from his position as a professor at JNU over sexual harassment allegations and accused the Congress of taking no action against him.“Despite the seriousness of the allegations, Congress has taken NO ACTION against him. Rahul Gandhi’s silence is deafening,” the party said.Earlier, addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, Swaraj described the allegations as “bone-chilling” and accused the Congress of hypocrisy over women's safety and empowerment."From media sources and media reports, the kind of allegations that have emerged are bone-chilling; they shake one's very soul. I would like to place before you the details of the kind of allegations that have surfaced. The Congress MP, who was a professor at JNU, asked sexually inappropriate questions to female students during assessments. It is alleged that he indulged in unwelcome physical contact with female students in JNU," Swaraj said.She further alleged that assessments were conducted at unusual hours at the MP's residence."Not only this, but media reports also reveal the allegation that this Congress MP used to call these female students to his home late at night to conduct academic assessments. He conducted one viva examination until 11:40 at night! And not just that-allegations of sexually explicit classroom conduct have also come to light. All of these are grave allegations," she stated.Earlier, Delhi Police registered an FIR following a complaint lodged by JNU's chief security officer, officials said.The FIR was registered on October 11 at Vasant Kunj North police station under Sections 75, 75(1)(i), 75(1)(iv) and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). According to the details of the FIR, Akoijam's name has been mentioned. Police said further investigation into the matter was underway.
Article Summary: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam accused of sexual harassment at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) BJP Mahila Morcha workers staged protests across the country on Monday, burning effigies of Rahul Gandhi. Protests followed reports that JNU had dismissed A Koijam from his position as a professor.

Article Title: No more a free circus, but a tamasha worth crores
Article Text:

The protest launched by Congress and left-wing student unions in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has posed several serious questions before the country’s political culture and democratic system. Congress and left-wing organizations have demanded the immediate removal of Gyanesh Kumar from the post of Chief Election Commissioner.A petition regarding this had also been filed in the Supreme Court. This petition demanded the removal of Gyanesh Kumar from his post. Even after the Supreme Court dismissed this petition, Congress’ Yuvraj Rahul Gandhi, along with his party’s MPs, has been wreaking havoc on the streets of Delhi every single day.There is a popular saying in Maharashtra, “Bin Paishacha Tamasha”, which means a tamasha born out of sheer foolishness that costs not even a penny. This surely entertains the onlookers. But the tamasha of the protest staged by the Congress and left-wing organizations is not free of cost; instead, it is costing crores of rupees every day. Paid protesters are being brought in. Unmasking the mastermind behind this multi-crore drama deserves a separate article.There is a competition going on between Rahul Gandhi and left-wing student unions to prove who is better in expressing fierce opposition to the Modi government by taking to the streets. When the footage of a young woman representing left-wing organizations climbing over a barricade and pushing women police officers went viral on social media, Yuvraj Gandhi felt a sudden urge to show just how brave he was. He began to fear that his own TRP might drop when this young woman was systematically brought into the limelight by left-wing organizations.It was out of this fear that he staged a protest march to the Chief Election Commissioner's office and satisfied his urge by climbing over police barricades. No country in the world has ever seen an opposition leader so childish, shallow and terrified for his very existence. Rahul Gandhi has sworn to tarnish the reputation of the office of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.He takes pride in bringing each and every Lok Sabha session to a standstill by creating a ruckus. Even though the Delhi Police have denied permission for the protest, Rahul Gandhi has become an expert at things like pushing down the police barricades and manhandling police officers. He is making a desperate attempt to prove himself as the Leader of the Opposition by acting like a Bollywood hero. He has destroyed his own reputation due to this frenzied behaviour.Rahul Gandhi does not have the intellectual capacity to understand that such cheap aggression does not help in politics. He should learn how to oppose a government from his grandmother Mrs. Indira Gandhi's life. The Janata Party government had appointed the Shah Commission to inquire into the atrocities committed during the Emergency.The Shah Commission found Indira Gandhi guilty. Subsequently, the police went to her home to arrest her. Mrs. Indira Gandhi surrendered to the police without any ruckus. But before that, she had called all the journalists and photographers in Delhi to her home. She calmly got herself arrested in front of them. She systematically gained the sympathy of voters through this. Now, that is what you call a shrewd politician.These days, Rahul Gandhi keeps on picking fights with the police over one thing or the other. His tactics, like marching towards the Prime Minister’s residence or attempting to enter the Election Commission’s office, show that he does not have even a basic understanding of politics. Even the common man has started to realise that Rahul Gandhi was just trying to get some publicity by trying to enter the Election Commission’s office without any prior appointment. Rahul Gandhi has decided to defy all parliamentary and government rules, conventions and laws.From a security perspective, security rules are extremely strict at places in Delhi such as Parliament House, Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Prime Minister’s residence etc. Rahul Gandhi must certainly be aware of the laws and rules, as he has been an MP for more than 22 years. Still, he is trying to break the law again and again. He is still not mature enough to understand that such gimmicks give temporary publicity, but do not make his leadership popular. In fact, it seems that he does not even want to develop such maturity.Not a single Congress leader currently has the courage to tell Rahul Gandhi, who has been criticizing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), that the Congress won in Kerala after this exercise was carried out. Rahul Gandhi, who accuses the EVMs of being manipulated, deliberately ignores the fact that he himself won an election by a margin of more than six lakh votes which was conducted using these very EVMs. He also conveniently forgets that the BJP won a majority when election was conducted through EVMs in 2014, when his own party was in power.Yuvraj is even failing to understand that such behaviour is causing him to lose his standing among the people. He is so obsessed with publicity that he has even forgotten that he is fighting against Narendra Modi and the Bharatiya Janata Party. He thinks that he is in competition with the youth who are gaining publicity by protesting in Delhi. He is not even bothered that he is adding to the difficulties faced by ordinary people in the Delhi region by staging protests every now and then and blocking roads. These protests can, at most, make him a reel star for a few days. He won’t get anything beyond that. Of course, he does not have the intellectual capacity to understand this. Therefore, there is no doubt that he will be more provocative and dramatic in the coming days.
Article Summary: The protest launched by Congress and left-wing student unions in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has posed serious questions before the country’s political culture and democratic system. The Congress has named it "Chalo Delhi - March for Democracy" and said participants will assemble at 1.30pm at the Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road junction.The opposition plans to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, demanding an end to alleged "vote chori", a halt to SIR and Kumar's resignation. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said peaceful citizens should not face illegal detention and that movement across Delhi must be allowed in accordance with the law.The court was hearing petitions challenging the police crackdown and detentions, along with a contempt plea alleging disobedience of its orders.Meanwhile, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital after he was allegedly manhandled by police during Sunday's protest. He later sought an independent investigation and accountability from the President, the Rajya Sabha chairman and the CJI.Brittas alleged that police personnel dragged him for around 50 metres, forcibly put him in a vehicle and assaulted him inside it before leaving him by the roadside. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta also criticised the opposition protests and praised Delhi Police for maintaining public safety.The latest confrontation follows the opposition's earlier march from Parliament to Vijay Chowk, after which INDIA bloc leaders submitted a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu. NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has rejected the INDIA bloc leaders’ request for a meeting to submit a representation on alleged “vote chori”, ANI reported on Sunday. In an email response to the opposition leaders, the CJI explained the reasons for declining their request.In response to the request the CJI said that the apex court cannot interfere with the executive’s functioning on the administrative side, sources told news agency PTI. He asked the Congress leader to file a petition on the judicial side, which could be taken up on Tuesday. The CJI also said the Supreme Court was open 24x7 to citizens whose fundamental rights were violated, PTI reported.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI between 4pm and 5pm on Monday to submit a memorandum demanding action over alleged electoral irregularities.Rahul had announced that opposition parties, civil society groups and young people would march to the Supreme Court, seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.The move to approach the CJI followed a meeting between INDIA bloc leaders and President Droupadi Murmu on Friday, during which the opposition submitted a memorandum outlining four demands.These included the CEC’s resignation, scrapping assembly elections held over the past two years, suspension of the SIR exercise and restoration of paper ballots. The memorandum also sought the restoration of 13.30 crore voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls.After the meeting, the Lok Sabha LoP said he was surprised that Murmu had not denied the opposition’s allegations of “vote chori” and had instead asked them to provide evidence. “I was shocked that the President did not deny Vote Chori. Instead, she asked us to bring her proof. We will bring her a mountain of it,” he wrote on X.The BJP subsequently attacked Gandhi over his remarks, accusing him of misrepresenting the interaction and dragging the President into a political confrontation. BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra called the Congress leader a “nalayak neta” and argued that accepting a memorandum did not amount to endorsing its contents.“The anarchist Rahul Gandhi tried to pull the President of India into the anarchism which he's trying his best to conduct on the streets of India,” Patra said.BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad also criticised the Opposition’s protests, saying the country would be governed by Parliament, not the streets. “We are not opposed to protests, but you have weaponised street protests because of your electoral defeats,” he said.

According to police, an argument broke out over the senior citizen seats after Singh and his son boarded the train at Mandi House. Sharma and his mother were seated on seats designated for senior citizens. “A dispute arose between Sharma and the father-son duo over the seat. The argument escalated into a physical altercation,” police said.When the train reached Supreme Court metro station, Sharma reportedly became unconscious. Information about an unconscious passenger on platform 1 was received at Supreme Court Metro police station around 5.47pm. By the time police reached LNJP Hospital, where Sharma had been taken with his mother, doctors had declared him brought dead,” a senior police officer said.Sharma had gone to Gurgaon with his mother to visit his brother and was returning home when the incident occurred. Sharma’s mother Durga claimed that when the metro reached the Supreme Court station, two men approached them. “They rudely asked us to vacate our seats. We got up, and my son then told them they could now lie down on the seats. The older man grabbed Pawan (Sharma) by the collar and slapped him. When he objected, the man’s son assaulted him. When I tried to intervene, the older man restrained my arm.”During the preliminary inquiry, police recorded the statement of Sharma’s mother. A case was registered based on her statement under Sections 105 and 3(5) of BNS, relating to culpable homicide not amounting to murder and acts committed with common intention.Investigators examined the circumstances surrounding the altercation and the alleged involvement of the two accused. Both men were arrested based on evidence collected during the investigation, police said. The accused were produced before a court and remanded to judicial custody for 14 days.
Article Summary: A 48-year-old man died following an alleged assault inside a Delhi Metro train over a seat reserved for senior citizens. The accused, Sanjay Pratap Singh and Sidharth Singh, both residents of Noida, have been remanded to 14-day judicial custody.

Article Title: 'Clear-cut violation': CJP’s Saurav Das claims 2 members detained, whereabouts unknown
Article Text:
In a post on X, Das said the party’s efforts to locate the two had been unsuccessful and that Balakrishna’s brother was extremely worried about his safety.





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das expressed concern over the whereabouts of party members Balakrishna and Sudhir, alleging that Delhi Police had detained them while they were peacefully protesting and had not informed the organisation about their location.In a post on X, Das said the party’s efforts to locate the two had been unsuccessful and that Balakrishna’s brother was extremely worried about his safety.He alleged that Delhi Police was keeping them incommunicado and refusing to allow them to contact their families or access a lawyer of their choice."We are very concerned about the safety of our organisation members Balakrishna and Sudhir. The Delhi Police had detained them today while they were peacefully protesting and their whereabouts are currently unknown. All our efforts to locate them have been in vain. Balakrishna’s brother is extremely worried about his life," Das wrote on X.“The Delhi Police is illegally keeping them in detention, incommunicado, and refusing to provide him a lawyer of his choice or let him contact his family members. This is a clear-cut violation of the Supreme Court’s order ,” Das said, adding that the party’s lawyers would move a contempt petition if their whereabouts were not disclosed immediately.The concerns came amid a press conference at the Press Club of India, where CJP leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Das questioned the police action against their members and thousands of protesters who had joined demonstrations at the party’s call.During the interaction with journalists, Das also raised concerns about the possible hacking of mobile phones seized during the detentions. He expressed apprehension that the devices could have been accessed or tampered with while in police custody.The press conference was attended by Ranka, Das, Singh, SFI member Aishe Ghosh and other Left-backed student activists.They raised questions about the action taken against the party and the protesters who had turned up in response to its call.The CJP has been demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The party has said it will continue its protest until Kumar resigns.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das expressed concern over the whereabouts of party members Balakrishna and Sudhir. He alleged that Delhi Police was keeping them incommunicado and refusing to allow them to contact their families or access a lawyer of their choice.

Article Title: Actor Imran Khan’s CJP protest participation under lens over 'OCI rules violation'
Article Text:
BJP’s Kirit Somaiya, who had flagged the alleged violation, said Khan is mentioned in a general FIR





MUMBAI: Police are in the process of writing to immigration officials over allegations that actor Imran Khan holds an overseas citizen of India card and had violated rules by participating in CJP’s stir on Saturday, said senior Gamdevi police inspector Prashant Mohite.BJP’s Kirit Somaiya, who had flagged the alleged violation, said Khan is mentioned in a general FIR but a separate case needs to be filed against him.He said he will visit the police station on Monday to ensure a separate FIR is lodged.
Article Summary: BJP’s Kirit Somaiya, who had flagged the alleged violation, said Khan is mentioned in a general FIR but a separate case needs to be filed against him. He said he will visit the police station on Monday to ensure a separate FIR is lodged.

Article Title: FIR against Congress MLA Jignesh Mevani over obstruction, rioting at Gujarat police station during poll campaign
Article Text:
Jignesh Mevani has come under legal scrutiny following a disturbance at the Pethapur police station during his election campaign

Mevani booked under multiple BNS sections

What does the FIR allege?





GANDHINAGAR: An FIR has been registered against Congress MLA Jignesh Mevani at Pethapur police station in Gujarat’s Gandhinagar over allegations of obstructing police personnel while they were recording a statement from a Congress candidate during the election campaign on October 9.According to the FIR, police were recording the candidate’s statement in connection with a complaint received against him when Mevani arrived at the police station with his supporters and allegedly obstructed personnel from discharging their duties.The FIR invokes several provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), including Section 189(2), which deals with punishment for unlawful assembly; Section 190, concerning joint liability for acts committed by members of an unlawful assembly; and Section 191(2), which relates to rioting.Other sections invoked include Section 221 for obstructing a public servant in the discharge of duties; Section 351(2) for criminal intimidation; and Section 352 for intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of peace.The FIR also includes Section 353(1)(b), concerning the spread of rumours or false statements intended to cause public fear or panic; Section 353(1)(c), concerning false information intended to incite one community or class to commit an offence against another; and Section 353(2), which deals with promoting enmity, hatred or ill-will between different groups on specified grounds.According to the FIR, the incident took place on October 9 at Pethapur police station in Gandhinagar during an election campaign.Police were recording a statement from a Congress candidate regarding a complaint received against him when Mevani allegedly arrived with his supporters and obstructed the officers in the discharge of their duties.Further details about the investigation and the allegations against Mevani were not available in the information provided.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Congress MLA Jignesh Mevani booked under multiple BNS sections. Incident took place on October 9 at Pethapur police station in Gandhinagar. Police were recording a statement from a Congress candidate regarding a complaint received against him. Allegedly arrived with his supporters and obstructed officers in the discharge of their duties.

Article Title: Mumbai Police book Aaditya Thackeray, Amit Thackeray after Shivaji Park protest
Article Text:
A case has been registered by the Mumbai Police against Aaditya Thackeray and Amit Thackeray

FIR over October 4 march at Azad Maidan





MUMBAI: Mumbai Police have registered a case against 25 people, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) leader Amit Thackeray, over a protest held outside Shivaji Park police station against the detention of demonstrators demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.The FIR also names MNS leader Sandeep Deshpande and Shiv Sena leaders Varun Sardesai and Mahesh Sawant. Police have invoked Section 189(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), relating to unlawful assembly, along with Sections 37(1), 37(3) and 135, in connection with the alleged violations of prohibitory orders.Aaditya and Amit staged the protest on Sunday, objecting to the detention of demonstrators who had taken to the streets over alleged irregularities in the electoral process.The protesters were demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Reacting to the detentions, Aaditya accused the BJP of being afraid of citizens protesting on the streets.“The BJP government is scared of Indian people, Indian citizens. And that's why you see they've been arresting every Indian who's a patriot coming out on the streets. BJP is scared.Those who ran away from us and joined the BJP, all those traitors, what are they saying now? Where is Eknath Shinde hiding? Where are the six MPs who went with him hiding? Where are all their allies?” he said.The latest action follows a separate FIR registered by Mumbai Police against organisers of a joint morcha held by MNS and Shiv Sena (UBT) on October 4.The case was filed at Azad Maidan police station after the march towards the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) headquarters was allegedly held without mandatory police permission and in violation of prohibitory orders in force in South Mumbai.The protesters had gathered to oppose CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Mumbai Police have registered a case against 25 people, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray. The protesters were demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over alleged discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

Article Title: ‘All a matter of demokursi’: Congress attacks PM Narendra Modi, HM Amit Shah over Jantar Mantar denotification
Article Text:
Congress general secretary in-charge, communications, Jairam Ramesh (File Photo)

(With Agency Inputs)





NEW DELHI: The Congress on Monday criticised Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the denotification of Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site, alleging that democracy no longer mattered to them and that it was all about “demokursi”.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said the move reflected “extreme panic” gripping the PM-HM duo, adding that the historic Jantar Mantar would no longer be a place where democracy received a daily booster dose."The poisonous pair is embattled, and we have seen in the past few days how brutally they have dealt with peaceful public protests," he said on X."Democracy no longer matters for them. It is all a matter of Demokursi," Ramesh added.His remarks came after the Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated site for protests and designated three new locations for demonstrations.In a standing order issued on October 11, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar named Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as the new designated protest sites.The move comes amid heightened security arrangements in the national capital following calls for protests at Jantar Mantar.
Article Summary: Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh said the move reflected “extreme panic” gripping the PM-HM duo. Delhi Police denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated site for protests and designated three new locations for demonstrations.

Article Title: 'Why not declare Mt Everest as protest site?': CJP's Ashutosh Ranka after Jantar Mantar de-notification
Article Text:
Dipke also criticised the move, alleging that Jantar Mantar had been turned into a “war zone”





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues in the national capital, prompting reactions from Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Abhijeet Dipke.Ranka questioned the decision in a post on X, asking, “Why not declare Mt Everest as the designated protest site?”Dipke also criticised the move, alleging that Jantar Mantar had been turned into a “war zone” and describing the decision as an attempt to restrict protests.“They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it’s no longer a protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!” Dipke tweeted.Under the new arrangement, Delhi Police has designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as alternative venues for protests and demonstrations.According to Standing Order No. 48/2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) constituted a committee to examine alternative venues where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.Based on the committee’s recommendations, Jantar Mantar has been removed from the list of designated protest venues, while the three locations have been designated for holding demonstrations.The order, issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar on October 11, partially modifies Standing Order No. 48/2022, dated April 28, 2022.
Article Summary: Delhi Police has removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest venues. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Abhijeet Dipke criticised the move. Delhi Police has designated Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as alternative venues for protests.

Article Title: Jantar Mantar no longer a designated protest site: Delhi Police names Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground as new venues for demonstrations
Article Text:
Delhi Police has removed Jantar Mantar from its list of designated protest venues, citing recommendations from a committee.





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated venue for protests and demonstrations, naming Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as the three alternative locations.According to Standing Order No. 48/2026, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) had constituted a committee to examine alternative venues where citizens could exercise their right to organise protests and demonstrations.Based on the committee’s recommendations, Jantar Mantar has been removed from the list of designated protest venues, while the three locations have been designated for holding demonstrations.Delhi Police said detailed standard operating procedures (SOPs) governing protests at the newly designated venues would be issued separately.The order, issued by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar on October 11, partially modifies Standing Order No. 48/2022, dated April 28, 2022.
Article Summary: Delhi Police has de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated venue for protests and demonstrations. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi are the three alternative locations. Delhi Police said detailed standard operating procedures (SOPs) governing protests at the newly designated venues would be issued separately.

Article Title: Mushrif and Patil lock horns over Gokul poll campaign inauguration
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:

chhapar fadake





Minister Hasan Mushrif and Congress MLC Satej Patil locked horns over the inauguration of the campaign for their respective panels for election to Kolhapur District Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul dairy.Mushrif is leading the panel of Mahayuti parties, while Satej Patil is leading the Samvichari panel. The campaign inauguration for their respective panels was held on Sunday. Mahayuti leaders gathered at Mahasainik Darbar Hall and leaders of the panel led by Satej Patil gathered in Chuye village of Karvir taluka, the birthplace of Anandrao Chuyekar, one of the founders of Gokul dairy.Mushrif said, "The opponents are contesting the election on false emotions. I am confident that all our 25 candidates are going to win. We are going to launch Mahayuti's manifesto soon and promises will be fulfilled in a timebound manner. The manifesto will deliberate upon the procurement prices of milk and nutrition of cattle. Our manifesto will provide things '' (windfall gains) for milk producers."Satej Patil said, "Mahayuti parties quarreled for six months and now they are showing false unity. They don't trust the delegates of milk producers, otherwise they would not ask them to take oath to show their allegiance. Our fight is for five and a half lakh farmers. We have released our manifesto which will be life-changing for farmers."The voting for Gokul dairy is scheduled to take place on Oct 18.
Article Summary: Hasan Mushrif and Congress MLC Satej Patil locked horns over the inauguration of the campaign for their respective panels for election to Kolhapur District Milk Producers Federation, popularly known as Gokul dairy.Mushrif is leading the panel of Mahayuti parties, while Patil leads the Samvichari panel.

Article Title: Rs 1 lakh bribe trap: Navi Mumbai ACB catches circle officer, talathi and woman assistant
Article Text:
The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite, Jaihind Birsha Koli (49) and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36).





NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe from a villager in Chirner, Uran taluka, to register the names of his relatives in the 7/12 extract of a land record.The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36), an assistant to the revenue officials.Dharmaraj Sonake, deputy superintendent of police, Navi Mumbai ACB, said the complainant had applied to register the names of the heirs of his deceased sister in the 7/12 extract of their land in Chirner.The land was jointly owned by the complainant's maternal uncle, aunt, brother and sister. The complainant had also applied for deletion of his deceased brother's name and submitted the request to circle officer Mohite and talathi Koli. However, the two officials allegedly demanded Rs 1 lakh from him to process the work.Dy SP Sonake said, "After verification of the complaint on Monday, when it was confirmed that the revenue officers Mohite and Koli had told the complainant to hand over the bribe amount to the accused woman assistant Monika Patil, a trap was laid on Tuesday around 2 pm. After the woman assistant Monika Patil accepted the demanded bribe of Rs 1 lakh from the complainant and handed it over to circle officer Keshav Mohite, both were caught red-handed and arrested. While, the acccused Talathi Jaihind Koli who was involved in the bribe demand was taken into custody from Dronagiri."
Article Summary: The Navi Mumbai Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB) has arrested two revenue officials and a woman assistant for allegedly accepting a Rs 1 lakh bribe. The arrested accused were identified as Keshav Dagdu Mohite (52), circle officer at Koproli in Uran taluka; Jaihind Birsha Koli (49), talathi; and Monika Vijnesh Patil (36)

Article Title: Man in Mahindra Thar with duplicate plate molests woman, knocks down another in Kharghar
Article Text:
30-year-old man was apprehended for allegedly molesting a woman and injuring another in Navi Mumbai.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team within 10 hours on Thursday evening.He had allegedly molested a 26-year-old woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night and, an hour later, severely injured a 22-year-old woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, Kharghar.Acting on a complaint by the woman allegedly molested by the Thar SUV driver, Kharghar police registered an FIR under BNS section 74 for the offence of assault or criminal force against a woman with the intent to outrage her modesty.While, as per the complaint by the injured woman Shrawani Dandekar, a resident of sector 3, Belpada, an FIR under relevant BNS sections and Motor Vehicle Act was registered against the Thar SUV driver for rash and negligent driving causing hurt.The detained aaccused identified as Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of sector 50, Seawoods, Nerul was handed over to Kharghar police for further legal action.Previously, in January 2021, he was arrested by Nerul police in the FIR registered against him for alleged kidnapping, sexual harassment and molestation of a woman.Sanjay Joshi, senior inspector of Kharghar said, "The accused Nakhvi has been detained and subsequently it will be decided whether to arrest him or serve with a notice under Bharatiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cooperating in police investigating."Audumbar Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-3 said, "After an FIR for molestation was registered at Kharghar police station by the victim woman, a resident of sector 34, Kharghar. As per the orders of higher authority, our team started a parallel probe. From the CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we obtained the red Thar SUV's registration number, which was of Vashi RTO passing.""When verified, the registration number was found to be that of a Maruti WagonR car. As the accused had used a duplicate registration number plate, we scrutinized as many as 62 Thar SUVs registered with various Regional Transport Offices (RTOs). Subsequently, we obtained the registration number of a red Thar SUV that was registered with Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar RTO," Patil added.SPI Patil further informed, "The SUV was registered in the name of Ali alias Talib Ahsan Nakhvi, a resident of Devaki Apartment in sector-50, Seawoods. From his mobile number registered with the RTO, his location was tracked.""He was apprehended from Bonkode village, Koparkhairane on Thursday late evening. Upon thorough interrogation, he confessed that he had inappropriately touched the woman pedestrian near Pethpada metro station while he drove his Thar SUV and sped away. He even confessed to have injured a woman pedestrian by hitting her his SUV while driving in Belpada area," he said.
Article Summary: A 30-year-old man wearing a mask and driving a red Thar SUV with a duplicate registration number plate was apprehended by the Crime Branch Unit-3 team on Thursday evening. He had allegedly molested a woman walking on the street in Kharghar, around 400metres from Pethpada metro station, on September 30 night. An hour later, he severely injured a woman by knocking her down in Belpada, Sector 3, KharGHar.

Article Title: 2 women escape from RPF lockup in Navi Mumbai; 1 held after 6 hours, cop suspended
Article Text:
The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. (AI image)





NAVI MUMBAI: In a major security lapse at Belapur Railway Protection Force (RPF), two women arrested for allegedly attempting to steal overhead electric wires from the Juinagar railway godown escaped from the lockup after midnight on September 28.One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large.The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated against her.As per the FIR registered by RPF sub-inspector Milap Parte (52) at Panvel GRP, a case was registered on September 24 under Section 3(a) of the Railway Property (Unauthorized Possession) Act, 1966, Amendment 2012, at Belapur railway police station.The case was based on a written memo submitted by RPF personnel Ravikant Gade regarding the theft of overhead electric wires from the godown at Juinagar railway station on September 21.During the probe, a trap was laid on September 26 and around 1pm, two women were found loitering suspiciously near the Juinagar godown with the alleged intention of committing theft.They were taken into custody and identified as Rupali Kailas Kurhade (30), from Jalna, and Shalibai Ashok Pawar (49), from Bhiwandi.They were arrested after an FIR was registered for attempted theft and produced before a CSMT court, which remanded them to police custody till September 30. They were lodged in the lockup at Belapur RPF police station.Day-shift woman constable Rakhi Malaiya was assigned guard duty at the lockup, after which woman head constable Pooja Bagre was on night duty.Around 2am on September 28, when Bagre had gone to the toilet, the two women allegedly managed to open the lock by inserting their hands through the iron bars of the lockup and jerking it. Police suspect the lock may not have been secured properly.The women then reached the balcony at the rear end of the police station. They removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping.The incident was captured on CCTV footage. PSI Parte learnt about the escape after waking up at home around 6.30am and finding several missed calls from head constable Bagre and ASI Rajiv Parsan.Sunil Nila, chief spokesperson of Central Railway, said, "One accused woman Rupali Kurhade was apprehended from near Nerul railway station around 8.45 am. The other accused Shalibai Pawar is still absconding."
Article Summary: The women removed their sarees, tied one end to the generator on the balcony and climbed down before escaping. One of them was apprehended around six hours later, while the other remains at large. The woman constable on night duty has been suspended and a departmental inquiry has been initiated.

Article Title: Thane Shiv Sena (UBT) leader murder: 2 more arrested near Alibag while fleeing to Goa, total 3
Article Text:
Two additional suspects were arrested in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena division chief Pradeep Purnekar.





THANE: The Thane Crime Branch has arrested two more accused in connection with the murder of Shiv Sena (UBT) division chief Pradeep alias Balu Purnekar, taking the total number of arrests in the case to three.The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa, according to police sources.The Crime Branch reportedly traced the duo following information obtained during the questioning of suspects detained earlier in the case. Police teams had been searching for the accused after Purnekar was shot and attacked with a sharp-edged weapon at his office in Thane.According to investigators, Yadav allegedly opened fire on Purnekar, while Pawar allegedly attacked him with a sharp weapon. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved in the alleged conspiracy.The two accused are expected to be produced before the Thane Sessions Court on Friday. Police will also attempt to recover the weapons allegedly used in the murder and investigate how the accused obtained them.Earlier, Prakash alias Papya Shinde was arrested in connection with the case. The police have also formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by DCP (Crime) Amarsingh Jadhav to conduct a detailed probe into the killing.The investigation is continuing, with police probing the alleged conspiracy, the role of other suspects and the possible involvement of the absconding accused.
Article Summary: The arrested accused have been identified as Nikhil Yadav and Nitesh Pawar alias Bhavdya. The two were apprehended near Alibag while allegedly attempting to flee towards Goa. Police are now expected to question both accused to establish the sequence of events, the motive and the role of others involved.

Article Title: Disha Salian case: Father, lawyer seek police protection, allege threats from Sena (UBT) leaders
Article Text:
Ojha questioned Aaditya Thackeray’s ‘Y-plus’ security, saying those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

(With agency inputs)





THANE: Advocate Nilesh Ojha on Sunday said that Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection, alleging that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Ojha, who is representing Satish Salian in the case, said they have written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the Chief Justice of India and Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis, seeking protection."The CBI FIR was registered, and a letter was immediately written requesting police protection for four individuals: Satish Salian, our witness Sameer Wankhede, myself, and Ashutosh Pathak, " Ojha told news agency ANI.Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray , saying those who brought the matter to light and allegedly faced threats had been left without protection."The letter clearly states, citing records from your Home Ministry and the Narcotics Bureau, that it is evident that Aditya Thackeray is involved in the drug trade. Furthermore, an FIR has now been registered against him regarding gang rape, murder, and a cover-up.Several other high-profile individuals and police officers are also implicated as accused in this matter," he said."We have already provided all prima facie evidence; the CBI has obtained everything necessary during the investigation to secure a conviction. Yet, the accused currently enjoys 'Y-plus' security provided by your administration. Meanwhile, those who brought this matter to light and those facing direct threats from individuals like Sanjay Raut were left unprotected," the advocate added.He further said that providing security was mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines, and alleged that their request for protection had not been acted upon.He further added, "Providing security is mandatory under the Witness Protection Scheme and Supreme Court guidelines. Yet, they failed to do so. Consequently, we compiled all the material and handed it over to the CBI. We also urged them to investigate the role of Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and determine why police protection was not granted.""We have given a copy of this to the CBI, along with Prime Minister Modi ji, the Home Minister, the Chief Justice of India, and the Chief Minister," Ojha said.Disha Salian was found dead in Mumbai on June 8, 2020. Her death was initially registered as an Accidental Death Report (ADR).Salian died days before actor Sushant Singh Rajput , whose death also led to a high-profile investigation and widespread public controversy.Bombay High Court directed the CBI to register a formal First Information Report (FIR) and launch a fresh probe.As the probe progresses, Satish Salian, accompanied by his lawyer Nilesh Ojha, has submitted a pen drive containing material they described as evidence related to Disha Salian’s death.Meanwhile, Aaditya Thackeray has denied the allegations and responded to the defamation notice issued by Satish Salian.
Article Summary: Disha Salian’s father, Satish Salian, Sameer Wankhede, Ashutosh Pathak and he have sought police protection. They allege that they received threats from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders. Ojha questioned the provision of ‘Y-plus’ security to Aaditya Thackeray. He said those who raised the issue and allegedly faced threats remained unprotected.

Article Title: Jalgaon police register case against road construction firm, engineer for death of 12-year-old in accident
Article Text:
Nashik:





Police have filed a case against a road construction company owner, a road engineer and a truck driver after a 12-year-old boy was killed and his father was seriously injured in an accident on Humbardi-Faizpur road in Jalgaon on Friday.Faizpur police identified the deceased boy as Lalit Kaviraj Chavan, a native of Burhanpur district in Madhya Pradesh who was residing in Anjala village in Yaval taluka. His father, Kaviraj, suffered serious injuries and is undergoing treatment.According to police, the father and son were travelling on a motorcycle from Faizpur towards Anjala around 7pm when a truck allegedly coming from the wrong side of the road crashed into their vehicle. The driver fled the spot without informing authorities or helping the victims. Lalit died from his injuries, while the motorcycle was badly damaged.Based on a complaint lodged by the injured man’s brother-in-law, police registered a case under Section 106(1) (causing death by negligence) and other relevant provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The complaint alleged that ongoing road construction work was being carried out without adequate safety measures, warning signs or precautions, creating a hazardous situation that contributed to the fatal accident.
Article Summary: A 12-year-old boy was killed and his father was seriously injured in an accident on Humbardi-Faizpur road in Jalgaon on Friday. Police have filed a case against a road construction company owner, a road engineer and a truck driver. The complaint alleged that ongoing road construction work was being carried out without adequate safety measures.

Article Title: Jalgaon police dispose of seized drugs worth Rs 65.7 crore
Article Text:
Disposal of Drugs by Jalgaon police

Nashik





: The Jalgaon police have disposed of narcotics worth Rs65.7 crore seized during two separate raids in the district.The contraband was transported from Jalgaon to M/s Maharashtra Enviro Power Ltd. at MIDC Ranjangaon in the Shirur taluka of Pune district on Friday. The transit took place under heavy police security, and the entire disposal process was video-recorded to maintain complete legal transparency.In July last year, the Jalgaon police seized over 43 kg of amphetamine worth Rs64.5 crore. The drugs were being transported in a car from Delhi to Bengaluru. The driver, who already had a case registered against him in Bengaluru approximately six years ago, was arrested. Acting on a tip-off about the drug smuggling operation, the Jalgaon police laid a trap, and the highway police intercepted the vehicle at Kannad Ghat.The Dhule rural police were called in for assistance and subsequently sought help from the forensic science department, which confirmed the substance was amphetamine. Following the confirmation, the car and contraband were seized, the driver was arrested, and a case was registered with the Chalisgaon rural police.Meanwhile, 884 grams of methaqualone were destroyed from a separate case registered with the Bhusawal Bazarpeth police station in 2024.The disposal of the drugs was carried out under the guidance of Jalgaon superintendent of police (SP) Srikant Dhivare.Officials stated that the destruction of seized narcotics is executed in accordance with Section 52-A of the NDPS Act, 1985, and its applicable rules. This protocol is strictly followed to prevent seized contraband from being stolen, resold illicitly, or re-entering the illegal market. The drugs are destroyed using controlled, high temperatures in an industrial furnace, ensuring the process causes no adverse effects on the air, water, or general environment.
Article Summary: The contraband was transported from Jalgaon to M/s Maharashtra Enviro Power Ltd. at MIDC Ranjangaon in the Shirur taluka of Pune district on Friday. The entire disposal process was video-recorded to maintain complete legal transparency. The drugs are destroyed using controlled, high temperatures in an industrial furnace.

Article Title: Hey Rahul, hello Modi: Vijay’s balancing act
Article Text:
modi & vijay

Chennai:





In less than 24 hours, chief minister C Joseph Vijay did a deft balancing act, hosting Congress leader Rahul Gandhi at his residence and sharing a metro ride with Prime Minister Narendra Modi .While his meeting with Rahul reinforced TVK’s partnership with Congress, his engagement with Modi signalled Vijay’s willingness to maintain a working relationship with the Union govt.After the metro ride, he accompanied Modi to the temple on IIT campus before sharing the stage with him at the event.While requesting the PM to sanction projects and funds, he also made it a point to thank him for announcing high-speed rail networks connecting Chennai with Hyderabad and Bengaluru in the Union budget.“If the state and Union govts work together, it will reflect in the welfare of the people,” Vijay said at the event.After a day-long engagements, Vijay also went to the airport to see off Modi.This is in sharp contrast to the past when Rahul would receive a rousing reception by DMK on his visits to Tamil Nadu, while Modi would be greeted with ‘Go Back’ slogans.“He was very cordial with the PM. This is what people of Tamil Nadu want and this is what would help the state grow,” said BJP spokesperson Narayanan Tirupathy.If Vijay’s lunch with Rahul dispelled speculations of discontent among a section of Congress due to TVK leaders pitching him as PM candidate, the Modi meeting reinforced Vijay’s conciliatory approach towards the Union govt.TVK functionaries said this would remain Vijay’s approach in the days ahead.This was the first time Modi and Vijay shared a stage. It was also Vijay’s first meeting with Rahul since TVK joined the INDIA bloc.Leaders of Congress and BJP welcomed Vijay’s approach, but said it was not a balancing act. Instead, they said, he has drawn a clear distinction between the two leaders.“Vijay met Rahul as a political leader, whereas he met PM Modi in his capacity as a CM,” said Congress leader A Gopanna. “TVK has an ideological bond with Congress. The two events cannot be compared,” he said.The challenge for Vijay, however, will be to keep both channels open in the long run without compromising the interests of TVK and its allies in TN. Vijay’s silence or muted response to key issues raised by Congress could come under scrutiny if not criticism, political observers said.Gopanna, however, said, “I don’t think Vijay would find this hard. If he has a difference with Modi, he would not hesitate to express it,” he said.
Article Summary: C Joseph Vijay hosted Rahul Gandhi at his residence and shared a metro ride with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. His engagement with Modi signalled Vijay’s willingness to maintain a working relationship with the Union govt. This is in sharp contrast to the past when Rahul would receive a rousing reception by DMK.

Article Title: SIT books 6th case against Veeramani
Article Text:
Pocso case

Chennai:





The Greater Chennai Police have registered one more case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenses (POCSO) Act against Gem Granites chairman R. Veeramani.The Special Investigation Team (SIT) registered the fresh case based on a complaint lodged by a mother alleging that her daughter was sexually abused when she was a minor. The child was earlier in the city, but later shifted to another district. This is the sixth case under the POCSO Act against Veeramani. He is also booked in a case of abetment of suicide involving a minor in 2004.Police sources said the investigators will take custody of Veeramani in the second POCSO Act case soon. Meanwhile, police launched a search at Veeramani’s residence on Lloyd’s Road in Royapettah based on specific information.Veeramani, along with a woman and her husband, was arrested on August 28 in the original investigation into allegations of sexual abuse of minor girls. The duo have been accused of facilitating the alleged abuse at a house rented by Veeramani. They were later detained under the Goondas Act. The accused would be formally arrested in all other cases, the sources said.
Article Summary: The Greater Chennai Police have registered one more case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offenses (POCSO) Act against Gem Granites chairman R. Veeramani. The Special Investigation Team (SIT) registered the fresh case based on a complaint lodged by a mother alleging that her daughter was sexually abused when she was a minor.

Article Title: 102 detained as DYFI, SFI, May 17 Movement stage black flag protests against Modi
Article Text:
Protests at Panagal Maligai

Chennai:





Police detained more than 100 protesters in Chennai and Coimbatore on Sunday as members of youth and student organisations staged black flag demonstrations against Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s visit to Tamil Nadu , demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and accusing the BJP-led Union govt of acting against the interests of the state and its people.In Chennai, the police detained 102 protesters from two separate demonstrations organised by Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and the May 17 Movement on Sunday, ahead of PM Modi’s visit to the city.Around 100 members of DYFI and SFI staged a black flag demonstration near Panagal Maligai in Saidapet, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and condemning alleged police excesses against protesters in Delhi.Holding black flags and chanting ‘Modi go back’ slogans, the protesters accused the BJP-led Union govt of electoral malpractice and questioned the Election Commission’s functioning. They also condemned the alleged detention of protesters in Delhi who had demanded accountability from election authorities.In a separate demonstration in T Nagar, around 70 members of the May 17 Movement staged a black flag protest against Modi’s visit, accusing the Union govt of pursuing policies detrimental to Tamil Nadu, Tamils and the Tamil language.Police detained 46 protesters. The protesters accused the Centre of withholding funds due to Tamil Nadu, promoting Hindi at the expense of Tamil and denying Metro rail projects to Coimbatore and Madurai.“Modi has visited Tamil Nadu 41 times, including 26 visits for government-related programmes. We have consistently protested against his visits because of his policies against Tamil Nadu and its people,” said Thirumurugan Gandhi, founder of the May 17 movement.The protesters also accused the BJP of attempting to saffronise Tamil poet Thiruvalluvar and alter his identity. They said Tamils revered Thiruvalluvar across religious and caste lines and that no political party had the right to appropriate his legacy.In Coimbatore, the SFI and DYFI staged a black-flag protest, marching from the district superintendent of police’s office and demonstrating near the exit of the district collectorate. Raising slogans such as “Narendra Modi, go back” and demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar, they carried black flags and placards reading “Go Back Modi” and “CBE Made It Clear, Gyanesh It’s Done, Bro”.DYFI district secretary Dinesh Raja condemned the alleged detention of students and youth during protests in Delhi. He demanded action against police personnel accused of assaulting protesters and urged the state govt to protect students’ democratic rights.Separately, around 20 people staged a protest at the district DMK office in North Coimbatore under the banner of “All Organisations”, led by Cockroach Janatha Party (CJP). They demanded the release of CJP founder Abhijeet Deepke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others.
Article Summary: More than 100 protesters detained in Chennai and Coimbatore. Demonstrators demand resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Protesters accuse Union govt of pursuing policies detrimental to Tamil Nadu, Tamils and the Tamil language. Police detained 46 protesters.

Article Title: TVK’s P Sathyabama wins Dharapuram byelection; Vijay party's Maragatham Kumaravel extends her lead in Madurantakam
Article Text:
TVK candidate P Sathyabama with party president and Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay





COIMBATORE/CHENNAI: TVK candidate P Sathyabama on Friday won the Dharapuram byelection by a margin of 9,471 votes, securing 66,841 votes.DMK candidate S Suganya came second with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK's K Banumathi secured 45,280 votes.The bypoll was necessitated after Sathyabama, who had won Dharapuram seat as an AIADMK candidate in the April assembly election, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK.Meanwhile, at the of 16th round of counting of votes in Madurantakam , TVK candidate Maragatham Kumaravel secured 63,391 votes, extending her lead over DMK candidate I Paranthaman (46,086 votes) to 17,305 votes. AIADMK candidate Kanitha Sampath remained in third place with 41,133 votes.Maragatham, who had won the Madurantakam seat as an AIADMK candidate in the last assembly election, resigned as MLAs and joined the ruling TVK, like Sathyabama.Polling was held in Dharapuram and Madurantakam on Oct 6.
Article Summary: TVK candidate P Sathyabama on Friday won the Dharapuram byelection by a margin of 9,471 votes, securing 66,841 votes. DMK candidate S Suganya came second with 57,370 votes, while AIADMK's K Banumathi secured 45,280 votes.
